newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futuris says GOI to sue over Elders bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futuris says GOI to sue over Elders bid.

text.p: Sir James Goldsmith's General Oriental Investments Ltd has told Futuris Corp Ltd it intends to sue Futuris over the Futuris bid for Elders Australia Ltd despite accepting the offer for its own stake in Elders, Futuris said on Wednesday.
Elders said earlier on Wednesday that GOI, which owns about seven percent of it, had accepted the offer.
Futuris, a diversified industrial group, had about 85 percent of Elders before GOI's acceptance.
Futuris is offering 10 of its shares for every nine Elders shares plus 23 cents per Elders share.

Futuris said that in a letter received by facsimile on Wednesday GOI contended that Futuris' statement of intent made prior to the bid and contained in its Part A statement that in the event of Elders not becoming a wholly owned subsidiary, Futuris intended to try to maintain the listing of Elders shares constituted a legally binding agreement with GOI.
GOI said it also constituted a representation to GOI and others.
Futuris said it disputed these claims and if proceedings were commenced, they would be vigorously defended.

Futuris said that on January 13 it wrote to GOI indicating that in view of the high level of acceptances, Futuris was concerned that the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) may not maintain the listing of Elders shares upon the bid closing.
Futuris said it confirmed to GOI by its letter that Futuris would "continue to negotiate with the ASX to try and achieve an early determination of the ASX's view".
In its letter on Wednesday, GOI asserted that the letter repudiated the alleged agreement, Futuris said.

"It has given notice that it intends to commence proceedings without further notice against the chief executive of Futuris, Mr Alan Newman, Futuris and other Futuris directors for alleged damages," Futuris said.

Futuris and its directors have taken advice their conduct did not give rise to any agreement, was not inconsistent with the representations contained in the Part A and that the letter of January 13 did not amount to any repudiation, it said.
Moreover, by accepting Futuris' bid GOI has not suffered damage and has not identified in any manner how any other alleged damage arises, Futuris said.
It said that upon acceptance by GOI, Futuris will be in a position to move to compulsory acquisition of all remaining Elders shares.
London-based Marathon Funds Management owns about eight of the Australian pastoral group.
Elders shares closed up 9.0 cents at A$2.20 while Futuris shares closed 5.0 cents up at A$1.86 following GIO's acceptance of the offer.
